data.name: About_Tagline
data.value: Modern fork of x360ce, rebuilt with SDL3, WPF, and .NET 10

data.name: About_Description
data.value: PadForge turns any input device into any virtual controller. Gamepads, joysticks, keyboards, mice, and touchscreens are mapped to virtual game controllers (Xbox, PlayStation, flight sticks, wheels, third-party gamepads) or keyboard+mouse / MIDI output that games treat as real hardware. Powered by HIDMaestro and Windows MIDI Services. It uses SDL3 for controller input, Windows Raw Input for keyboard and mouse, HidHide for per-game device masking, and provides a modern Fluent Design interface for mapping, deadzones, sensitivity curves, and force feedback.

data.name: About_MidiServicesDesc
data.value: Virtual MIDI device output (Windows MIDI Services)

data.name: About_ZackslyIconsDesc
data.value: Stick and trigger icons derived from "Xbox Series Button Icons and Controls" by Zacksly (CC BY 3.0)

data.name: About_QDollarDesc
data.value: Touchpad shape-template matcher (Circle / Square / Triangle / Z / Checkmark and custom recorded gestures). C# re-derivation of the JavaScript reference by Magrofuoco, Vatavu, Anthony, and Wobbrock. BSD 3-Clause.

data.name: About_GestureSignDesc
data.value: Angular-margin scoring approach that runs alongside the point-cloud matcher on single-finger shapes. Adapted from GestureSign's PointPatternAnalyzer. BSD 3-Clause.

data.name: About_LicenseText
data.value: This software is licensed under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International). 3D controller models adapted from Handheld Companion (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0). 2D controller assets from Gamepad-Asset-Pack by AL2009man (MIT). Original codebase forked from x360ce (MIT). SDL3 is licensed under the zlib License. HIDMaestro, Windows MIDI Services, HidHide, HelixToolkit, and WPF UI are licensed under the MIT License. OpenXInput ships only an upstream trademark disclaimer. Redistributed as-is under the same terms. $Q Recognizer (Magrofuoco / Vatavu / Anthony / Wobbrock) and GestureSign's PointPatternAnalyzer (TransposonY) are both licensed under the BSD 3-Clause License. PadForge's touchpad ShapeRecognizer and AngularMarginRecognizer are C# re-derivations of those references.

data.name: Pad_ImpulseTriggers_Subtitle
data.value: Forwards per-trigger motor commands (Xbox Impulse Triggers) from the virtual controller to the assigned physical Xbox One, Elite, or Series controller. Game-driven trigger rumble passes through automatically. The controls below scale the magnitude per trigger.

data.name: Pad_ImpulseTriggers_SwapTriggers
data.value: Swap left and right trigger motors

data.name: Pad_ConstantTriggerForce_Description
data.value: Apply a continuous force to each trigger motor until you toggle off. Game-driven trigger force from any source overrides while it's active and resumes when the game stops.

data.name: Pad_AudioTriggerRumble_Description
data.value: Drive the trigger motors from system audio bass. Game-driven trigger force overrides while it's active.

data.name: Pad_AdaptiveTriggers_Subtitle
data.value: Configure trigger feedback effects on the assigned physical DualSense. Game-driven trigger effects are forwarded automatically. Settings here add a user-configured layer that runs when no game is writing.

data.name: Pad_Sticks_Subtitle
data.value: Per-stick deadzones, anti-deadzones, sensitivity curves, and center-offset calibration. Each section below targets one analog stick on the active output. Extended profiles can have up to four sticks. Standard gamepads have two.

data.name: Pad_Triggers_Subtitle
data.value: Per-trigger deadzones, anti-deadzones, max-range scaling, and sensitivity curves. Each section below targets one trigger axis on the active output. Extended profiles can expose up to eight axes shared with the Sticks tab.

data.name: Pad_ForceFeedback_Subtitle
data.value: Tunes how PadForge scales force feedback events from the game and how it routes them to the physical controller's rumble motors or haptic actuators. Audio Rumble adds a system audio-driven layer on top.

data.name: Pad_AT_Feedback_Tooltip
data.value: Constant resistance from the start position to fully pressed. Strength sets how hard the trigger pushes back.

data.name: Pad_AT_Weapon_Tooltip
data.value: Gun-trigger feel. Pull through a soft zone to the end position, then a firm click. Use start/end to set the click point and strength for the click force.

data.name: Pad_AT_Vibration_Tooltip
data.value: Continuous buzz once you cross the start position. Frequency sets the pulse rate. Strength sets the intensity.

data.name: Pad_AT_MultiPosFeedback_Tooltip
data.value: Ratcheting resistance. Discrete force bumps across the start-to-end range. Pulling the trigger feels like clicking through detents instead of pushing through one continuous wall.

data.name: Pad_AT_Slope_Tooltip
data.value: Resistance ramps from light at the start position to full at the end position. Past the end position the trigger holds at peak strength.

data.name: Pad_AT_MultiPosVibration_Tooltip
data.value: Stuttering vibration. Short buzz bursts spaced across the start-to-end range. Pulling the trigger feels like crossing distinct vibration zones, not one continuous buzz.

data.name: Pad_AT_LoadGameCubePreset_Tooltip
data.value: Fills Range and Strength with values that match the physical click-feel of a real GameCube trigger (start ~56%, end ~63%, max force). Tweak the sliders afterwards if you want a different feel.

data.name: Pad_Lighting_Subtitle
data.value: Set the lightbar base color and audio behavior on the assigned physical controller. Game writes always win. User settings apply when no game is driving the lightbar.

data.name: Pad_Lighting_BaseEnabled
data.value: Apply user-configured base color when no game is writing

data.name: Pad_Lighting_HexTooltip
data.value: Enter a six-digit hex color (RRGGBB or #RRGGBB) and press Enter or click away to apply.

data.name: Pad_Lighting_RemoveColor
data.value: Remove this color from the palette

data.name: Pad_Lighting_PlayerLeds_Subtitle
data.value: Five small white LEDs below the touchpad. Pick which player slot pattern to display and how bright it should be.

data.name: Pad_Lighting_IndicatorLeds_Subtitle
data.value: Player number row (5 LEDs below the touchpad) and the mute LED above the mic. The brightness control physically only affects the player row. The firmware exposes mute LED states (Off / Solid / Pulse) but no separate mute brightness register.

data.name: Pad_Lighting_AudioLightbar_Subtitle
data.value: Modulates the base color above by the system audio peak. Pulses with whatever is playing through the default output device. Taps into the same WASAPI capture as audio rumble but reads the full waveform (no bass-cutoff filter), so it follows everything you hear.

data.name: Pad_Lighting_AudioLightbar_Enable
data.value: Pulse base color with system audio

data.name: Pad_Lighting_Mode_AudioPulseRandom
data.value: Audio Pulse — Random Color per Beat

data.name: Pad_Lighting_Mode_AudioThresholds
data.value: Audio Bands — Three Colors, Hard Transitions

data.name: Pad_Lighting_Mode_AudioGradient
data.value: Audio Bands — Three Colors, Smooth Gradient

data.name: Pad_Lighting_Mode_AudioCrossFade
data.value: Audio Bands — Three Colors, Crossfade at Boundaries

data.name: Pad_Lighting_Mode_InputReactive
data.value: Input Reactive — Random Color per Press

data.name: Pad_Lighting_Mode_InputReactiveFixed
data.value: Input Reactive — Single Color per Press

data.name: Pad_Lighting_ResetPaletteTooltip
data.value: Replace the current palette with the four default colors (red, green, blue, yellow).

data.name: ImportFromDevice_Description
data.value: Pick a connected HID device. PadForge captures its descriptor, identity, and layout and saves it as a new Extended profile named "(User Generated)". The profile lives inside PadForge.xml so it travels with your settings.

data.name: ManageProfiles_Description
data.value: User-imported HIDMaestro profiles are stored inside PadForge.xml and appear in every Extended slot's profile dropdown. Capture a new one from a connected device below, or export / delete an existing one.

data.name: Pad_ExtendedCustomizeTooltip
data.value: Enable the identity and layout override fields below. When off, the virtual controller uses the selected profile's built-in identity and HID descriptor exactly as shipped by HIDMaestro.

data.name: Pad_ExtendedResetDefaultsTooltip

data.name: Pad_ExtendedProductStringTooltip

data.name: Pad_ExtendedOemOverrideTooltip
data.value: Claim the Windows DirectInput OEM-name table entry for this profile's VID:PID. joy.cpl and DirectInput UIs normally read that table before the HID iProduct string. Enable this so the Product String above wins. Off by default.

data.name: Pad_Mapping_Up_IconTooltip

data.name: Pad_Mapping_Up_PickerTooltip

data.name: Pad_Mapping_Down_IconTooltip

data.name: Pad_Mapping_Down_PickerTooltip
data.value: Down: button that ramps the accumulator downward while held.

data.name: Pad_Mapping_Rate_Tooltip
data.value: Sweep speed in units per second. 0.5 = full range in 2 s; 2 = full range in 0.5 s.

data.name: Pad_Mapping_Sticky_Tooltip
data.value: When checked, the accumulator holds its value after release (cruise control). When unchecked, it snaps back to Min on release.

data.name: Pad_Mapping_Min_Tooltip
data.value: Lower bound of the accumulator. -1 = full negative for bipolar axis targets; 0 = unipolar.

data.name: Pad_Mapping_Max_Tooltip

data.name: Pad_Mapping_Modifier_IconTooltip

data.name: Pad_Mapping_Modifier_PickerTooltip
data.value: Modifier: while held, the row's output flips sign.

data.name: Pad_Mapping_AddSource_Tooltip
data.value: Add another physical input to this row

data.name: Pad_Combine_Tooltip
data.value: How to merge sources on this row.

data.name: Pad_Combine_MaxAbs_Description
data.value: Use whichever source has the strongest push

data.name: Pad_Combine_OR_Description
data.value: Fire when any source is active. Good for buttons.

data.name: Pad_Combine_AND_Description
data.value: Fire only when all sources are active

data.name: Pad_Combine_XOR_Description
data.value: Fire only when exactly one source is active

data.name: Pad_Combine_Custom_Description
data.value: Build your own with the formula editor below

data.name: Pad_Formula_TextBox_Tooltip
data.value: Click chips below to build a formula, or drag chips into the box. a, b, c… stand for this row's sources in order.

data.name: Pad_Formula_Chip_TouchpadFlag_A
data.value: 1 while source A is touching (touchpad passthrough rows only)

data.name: Pad_Formula_Chip_Clamp
data.value: Keep within a range: clamp(value, low, high)

data.name: Pad_Formula_Chip_Lerp
data.value: Blend two values: lerp(a, b, mix0to1)

data.name: Pad_Formula_Preset_CapTo1_Tooltip
data.value: Sum A + B but never exceed ±1

data.name: Pad_Formula_Preset_AUnlessIdle_Tooltip
data.value: Use A, but if A is at rest, fall back to B

data.name: Pad_Formula_Preset_ThresholdGate_Tooltip
data.value: Fire fully if A is past halfway, otherwise zero. Turns an axis into a button.

data.name: Pad_Formula_Preset_BothPressed_Tooltip
data.value: Fire only when A and B are both pushed

data.name: Pad_Formula_Preset_StrongerWins_Tooltip
data.value: Whichever of A or B is pushed harder, with sign

data.name: Pad_Mapping_ExtraSourcePickerTooltip
data.value: Pick the source from any device assigned to this slot.

data.name: Pad_Mapping_AddOppositeDir_Tooltip
data.value: Only the positive (+) direction of this stick axis is mapped. Click to add an inverted second source for the negative (−) direction.

data.name: Pad_Formula_Error_SingleEqualsNotSupported
data.value: Single '=' not supported at {0}. Use '==' for equality.

data.name: Macro_Expression_Tooltip
data.value: Reference variables as a, b, c, … (or s[0], s[1], …). Supports + - * / && || ?: and abs/min/max/clamp/sign/lerp. The macro fires on the rising edge when the formula's value crosses 0.5.

data.name: Macro_Expression_Hint
data.value: Each row defines one variable letter (a, b, c, …). Choose Input Device to bind a button, POV, or axis on a physical device, or Output Controller to read a channel on the slot's combined virtual controller output.

data.name: Macro_Expression_Recipe_Single_Tooltip
data.value: Fire when variable a goes from 0 to 1.

data.name: Macro_Expression_Recipe_Both_Tooltip
data.value: Fire only when both a AND b are active. Classic chord.

data.name: Macro_Expression_Recipe_Either_Tooltip
data.value: Fire when either a OR b is active.

data.name: Macro_Expression_Recipe_AButNotB_Tooltip
data.value: Fire when a is active and b is NOT active.

data.name: Macro_Expression_Recipe_AxisOverHalf_Tooltip
data.value: Fire when stick axis a is deflected more than 50% from rest.

data.name: Macro_AlwaysDesc
data.value: Runs continuously while this virtual controller is active. No trigger button required.

data.name: Macro_KeyComboHint
data.value: Select a key to add it. Example: {Control}{Alt}{Delete}

data.name: Macro_ProcessTooltip
data.value: Process name without .exe. Dropdown shows processes with active audio sessions.

data.name: MacroAction_LightbarColor_Tooltip
data.value: Override the assigned PlayStation slot's lightbar to a chosen RGB color. Reactive fades from full intensity to black over the configured decay window, then hands back to the Lighting tab's settings. Sticky holds the color until a Clear Lightbar Override action runs. Game-driven writes still take priority over the override.

data.name: MacroAction_LightbarColorClear_Tooltip
data.value: Releases any active lightbar override on the assigned slot. Pair with a Sticky Set Lightbar Color action to undo it via another macro.

data.name: MacroAction_LightbarModeSet_Tooltip
data.value: Sets the assigned slot's lightbar mode to a specific value. Persists like a Lighting tab edit until another action or the user changes it.

data.name: MacroAction_LightbarModeCycle_Tooltip
data.value: Advances the slot's lightbar mode through the modes selected below. Each fire moves to the next checked mode. The cycle position is per-action and resets on app restart.

data.name: Macro_LightbarPalette_Empty
data.value: Empty palette uses the slot's own Lighting tab palette.

data.name: Macro_LightbarCycleModes_Hint
data.value: Pick which lightbar modes the macro should cycle through. Each fire advances to the next checked mode.

data.name: MacroAction_Rumble_Tooltip
data.value: Drives the slot's physical device rumble from a macro. Reactive runs at full strength for the hold window then fades to zero across the fade window. Sticky holds at full strength until a Stop Rumble action runs. Layers on top of game-driven rumble via max() so user-driven feedback is always felt.

data.name: MacroAction_RumbleStop_Tooltip
data.value: Releases any active rumble override on the assigned slot. Pair with a Sticky Rumble action to undo the hold via another macro.

data.name: Macro_SetGyroEngaged_Tooltip
data.value: Sets the slot's gyro engage state from a macro. Toggle flips the current state. On forces gyro engaged. Off forces it disengaged. Independent of the Gyro tab's engage button. The two sources OR-combine, so neither can disable what the other engaged.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_Subtitle
data.value: Per-touchpad input. Gestures (swipes, taps, pinches, shapes) and continuous output modes (virtual stick / D-pad, mouse) become mapping sources you can bind on the Mappings tab.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_GesturesEnabled_Tooltip
data.value: Master toggle for this touchpad. When off, no gesture descriptors fire for this touchpad. Existing finger / click / position mappings still work.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_Mode_Tooltip
data.value: Which gesture catalog the engine evaluates against the live finger paths. "Both" is the default.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_CooldownMs_Tooltip
data.value: After a gesture fires, ignore new gestures on this touchpad for this many milliseconds. Prevents bounce-fires from rapid back-and-forth motion.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_RadialZones_Tooltip
data.value: Slide outward from your finger's landing point into a wedge. Zone 0 anchors at the top and zones increase clockwise. Each zone's entry in the picker shows its direction in parentheses as degrees from the top: (0°) is up, (90°) is right, (180°) is down, (270°) is left. Only one zone is held at a time. Sliding into another releases the previous one, so you can cycle through zones in a single swipe.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_ShapeGestures
data.value: Shape Gestures (Circle, Square, Triangle, Z, Checkmark)

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_Custom_Empty
data.value: No custom gestures recorded for this profile. Click Record New Gesture to capture one.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_Stick_Subtitle
data.value: Turn the touchpad into a virtual analog stick or D-pad. The output anchors where your finger first lands. Current position relative to that anchor drives the stick value and (optionally) latched D-pad direction bools.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_StickEnabled_Tooltip
data.value: Surfaces Touchpad Stick X, Stick Y, and D-Pad descriptors in the mapping picker. Works alongside the existing touchpad-finger and touchpad-gesture sources, not instead of them.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_StickDPadMode_Tooltip
data.value: Off skips D-pad output. 4-Way emits one cardinal at a time. 8-Way emits two cardinals for diagonals (the same way physical D-pads report NE / NW / SE / SW).

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_Mouse_Subtitle
data.value: Tunes cursor speed when a touchpad finger is mapped to mouse X/Y on a Keyboard / Mouse virtual controller. 1.0 is the default. Raise either axis for a faster cursor, lower for slower. Invert flips either axis.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_MouseSensitivityX_Tooltip
data.value: Multiplier on horizontal touchpad → mouse delta. Below 1.0 slows the cursor. Above 1.0 speeds it up.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_MouseSensitivityY_Tooltip
data.value: Multiplier on vertical touchpad → mouse delta.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_MouseInvertX_Tooltip
data.value: Flip horizontal motion. Finger right moves the cursor left.

data.name: Pad_Touchpad_MouseInvertY_Tooltip
data.value: Flip vertical motion. Finger down moves the cursor up.

data.name: Pad_ResetTouchpadTaps
data.value: Reset Tap / Double Tap / Triple Tap

data.name: Recorder_Subtitle
data.value: Draw the gesture on the surface below. The dialog captures every finger you put down. When you take all fingers off the surface the sample is recorded. Drawing a different finger count from previous samples resets the stack.

data.name: Recorder_Waiting
data.value: Waiting for finger contact on the canvas

data.name: Recorder_Waiting_Device
data.value: Draw on the touchpad. The canvas mirrors it live.

data.name: Recorder_TargetDevice_None
data.value: Touchpad unavailable. Use the canvas below with mouse or touch.

data.name: Recorder_Complete
data.value: All samples captured. Name the gesture and click Save.

data.name: Recorder_SampleCount_Hint
data.value: 3 is the standard. More samples = sturdier match, fewer = faster recording.

data.name: Recorder_Error_NoEngine
data.value: Engine not running. Start the engine before recording.

data.name: Recorder_Error_BadSample
data.value: No valid sample captured. Try drawing the gesture again.

data.name: Settings_GyroCalibrate_Tooltip
data.value: Place the controller on a flat surface and click Calibrate Gyro to sample the at-rest reading for ~1.5 seconds. Subtracted from raw readings so gyro mappings don't drift the mouse / stick when the controller is still.

data.name: Settings_GyroResetCalibration_Tooltip
data.value: Clears the at-rest gyro bias and the last-calibrated timestamp. The next polling cycle re-runs the 1.5-second auto-calibration on this device.

data.name: Settings_GyroSensitivityH_Tooltip
data.value: Scales the horizontal (Yaw + Roll) gyro contribution to the output. 1.0 leaves the rate as the engine sees it. Higher values amplify, lower values attenuate. Apply at the device level so every gyro binding on this controller inherits the same horizontal feel.

data.name: Settings_GyroSensitivityV_Tooltip
data.value: Scales the vertical (Pitch) gyro contribution to the output. Separate from horizontal so you can tune aim X and Y independently.

data.name: Settings_GyroDeadZone_Tooltip
data.value: Minimum rotation rate (degrees per second) below which gyro output is treated as zero. Rejects at-rest hand tremor without snapping behavior. Rates past the threshold pass through with the threshold subtracted.

data.name: Settings_GyroSmoothing_Tooltip
data.value: Single-pole EMA filter on the gyro rate. 0 = off (raw signal, lowest latency). Higher values reduce per-frame jitter at the cost of added lag. 0.5 is a reasonable starting point if the cursor feels twitchy.

data.name: Settings_GyroAcceleration_Tooltip
data.value: Rate-dependent gain. 0 = off (linear scaling). Higher values let slow movements pass through unchanged while amplifying fast movements. Useful for combining precision aim with quick turns.

data.name: Settings_GyroOutputCurve_Tooltip
data.value: Reshapes the response. Linear = pass-through. Aggressive = x² (slow stays slow, fast amplifies). Relaxed = √x (slow amplifies, fast saturates). Wide / ExtraWide sit between aggressive and saturated. Composes with Acceleration.

data.name: Settings_GyroSensitivityUnits_Tooltip
data.value: Sensitivity unit display. Multiplier is the internal × scale (1 = baseline). DegPerScreenTurn is Steam-style: degrees of physical controller rotation per one full screen turn.

data.name: Settings_GyroEasyAimThreshold_Tooltip
data.value: Right-stick deflection (0–100%) below which gyro output is zeroed. 0 = always on. Steam's "gyro engaged while aiming" feel. Gyro fires only when the user pushes the right stick past the threshold.

data.name: Pad_Gyro_Subtitle
data.value: Tune how this pad's motion sensor drives mouse and stick output. Calibrate on a flat surface to zero at-rest drift, then dial in sensitivity, smoothing, and engage rules to taste.

data.name: Pad_Gyro_EasyAim_Subtitle
data.value: Engage gyro only while the right stick is deflected. 0% disables (gyro always-on).

data.name: Settings_GyroSpace_Tooltip
data.value: How gyro motion is interpreted. Local uses the raw controller axes. Player projects horizontal motion onto the real-world vertical (gravity) so the same wrist twist always turns the camera, regardless of how you hold the pad. World additionally re-projects vertical motion onto world axes.

data.name: Settings_GyroInvertPitch_Tooltip
data.value: Flips the pitch axis. Applies after the gyro space projection, independently of any per-source invert flags on the mapping table.

data.name: Settings_GyroInvertYawRoll_Tooltip
data.value: Flips the yaw axis. Also covers the roll and horizontal-blend gyro sources.

data.name: Settings_GyroRealWorldCalibration_Tooltip
data.value: In-game degrees per physical degree of controller rotation. 0 turns this off. 1.0 means a 90° wrist rotation produces a 90° camera turn. Calibrate once per game: rotate the pad a full turn and adjust until the in-game camera also rotates a full turn.

data.name: Settings_GyroTightening_Tooltip
data.value: Below this rotation rate, the input is fully replaced by the smoothing buffer's average. Drops hand tremor and microscopic drift. Default 3°/s.

data.name: Settings_GyroSmoothingThreshold_Tooltip
data.value: Above this rotation rate, the input passes through raw so fast turns retain precision. Between the tightening and smoothing thresholds, a linear ramp blends the two. Default 8°/s.

data.name: Settings_GyroSmoothingWindow_Tooltip
data.value: Length of the smoothing-buffer time window. Larger values smooth more heavily below the tightening threshold. Smaller values feel snappier. Default 50ms.

data.name: Settings_GyroAimEngageButton_Tooltip
data.value: Button that gates gyro output. Gyro fires only while this button is held. Leave unset to disable the button gate. When both this and the right-stick deflection are configured, both must be active for gyro to fire.

data.name: Settings_GyroAimEngageMode_Tooltip
data.value: Hold: gyro fires while the engage button is held. Toggle: each press flips gyro on or off, and release does nothing. Toggle is sticky across the polling tick and resets on profile switch.

data.name: Pad_Gyro_Engage_Subtitle
data.value: Optional gates that limit when gyro is active. Right-stick deflection and the aim engage button can each be configured. Gyro fires only while every configured gate is active.

data.name: Pad_Gyro_AimEngage_Record
data.value: Record the next physical input press as the aim engage button

data.name: Pad_Gyro_ApplyToPassthrough
data.value: Apply Gyro Tuning to Motion Passthrough

data.name: Pad_Gyro_ApplyToPassthrough_Tooltip
data.value: Runs this tab's discretionary gyro tuning (deadzone, sensitivity, smoothing, response curve, invert) on the motion the virtual controller reports to the game or emulator. Turn it off to send only the calibrated reading and let the game apply its own sensitivity and smoothing. Calibration drift correction always applies either way.

data.name: Mapping_GyroSensitivity_Tooltip
data.value: Per-source gyro sensitivity multiplier. 1.0 = the engine's default (500°/s → full deflection). Values above 1.0 are more sensitive. Values below 1.0 are less sensitive.

data.name: Profiles_Description
data.value: Create per-application controller profiles that auto-switch based on the active game.

data.name: Profiles_AutoSwitch
data.value: Auto-switch profiles based on foreground application

data.name: CopyFrom_SelectDevice
data.value: Select a device to copy its settings from:

data.name: Pad_SensitivityCurveHint
data.value: Double-click chart to add point. Right-click to remove. Drag to adjust.

data.name: Pad_SensitivityCurveHintShort
data.value: Double-click to add point. Right-click to remove. Drag to adjust.

data.name: Pad_ConstantForce_Description
data.value: Apply a continuous force to this device until you toggle off. Game-driven force from any source overrides while it's active and resumes when the game stops.

data.name: Pad_ConstantForce_Position
data.value: Drag inside the grid to set direction and strength.

data.name: Macro_RecordHint
data.value: Press buttons or move an axis/trigger to record. Axes are detected when deflected past 50%.

data.name: Pad_Either_Tooltip
data.value: When Half is on, fire on deflection past the deadzone in either direction from center (Invert has no effect).

data.name: Macro_SysVolumeHint
data.value: Continuously maps the selected axis (0–100%) to the Windows system volume, scaled to the volume limit. Use with "Always" trigger, or a button/axis trigger with "While Held" + "Until Release".

data.name: Macro_AppVolumeHint
data.value: Controls the volume of a specific application in the Windows volume mixer, scaled to the volume limit. Enter the process name (visible in Task Manager). Use with "Always" trigger, or a button/axis trigger with "While Held" + "Until Release".

data.name: Macro_MouseMoveHint
data.value: Continuously maps the selected axis to mouse movement (or scroll). Use with "Always" trigger, or a button/axis trigger with "While Held" + "Until Release". For stick-to-mouse, create two actions: one for X axis, one for Y axis.

data.name: Settings_AudioRumbleDesc
data.value: Drive controller rumble from system audio bass frequencies.

data.name: Settings_HmInactivityTimeoutTooltip
data.value: Seconds before a virtual controller is destroyed when all mapped devices are offline. 0 disables. Surviving controllers shift up to fill the gap and re-bind to lower XInput slots.

data.name: Pad_Shift_AddLayer_Tooltip
data.value: Add a shift layer. A second mapping table that activates while a button is held or toggled.

data.name: Pad_Shift_HintNameDuplicate
data.value: A layer with that name already exists on this slot.

data.name: Pad_Shift_Icon_Tooltip
data.value: Pick an emoji to show on the flyout when this layer is engaged.

data.name: Pad_Shift_DeleteConfirm_Format
data.value: Delete the "{0}" layer and all of its mapping rows? This cannot be undone.

data.name: Pad_Shift_NoInherit_Tooltip
data.value: When checked, this layer's target stays OFF instead of falling through to the Base row.

data.name: Pad_Shift_Delay_Tooltip
data.value: Milliseconds the activator must stay engaged before the layer change fires.

data.name: Pad_Shift_KindButton_Subtitle
data.value: A single button (or POV direction) press engages the layer.

data.name: Pad_Shift_KindChord_Subtitle
data.value: Both buttons must be held simultaneously to engage. Cross-device chord supported.

data.name: Pad_Shift_KindAxis_Subtitle
data.value: Engages while an analog axis is past the threshold value.

data.name: Pad_Shift_ModeHold_Subtitle
data.value: Layer stays engaged while the activator is held. Releases when you let go.

data.name: Pad_Shift_ModeToggle_Subtitle
data.value: Tap to engage. Tap again to release. Layer persists across many presses.

data.name: Pad_Shift_ModeCustom_Subtitle
data.value: Press jumps to a specific layer. Stays until another transition fires.

data.name: Pad_Shift_ModeCycle_Subtitle
data.value: Each press advances through an ordered layer list. Wraps back to Base.

data.name: Pad_Shift_ModeSticky_Subtitle
data.value: Tap once to engage. The next mapped button press fires on the layer, then auto-releases.

data.name: Pad_Shift_PostponeMapping_Tooltip
data.value: When checked, the activator button still drives any row that uses it as a source. One press both changes layer AND fires the button's own mapping. When unchecked (default), the activator press is consumed by the layer change only.

data.name: Pad_Shift_InheritUnmapped_Tooltip
data.value: When checked, targets this layer doesn't explicitly map fall through to the Base layer. When unchecked (default), the layer replaces Base entirely and unmapped targets stay off.

data.name: Pad_Steering_Subtitle
data.value: Off leaves this a normal stick. The other modes make it steer like a wheel.

data.name: Pad_Steering_LockFeedback_Subtitle
data.value: Make the wheel feel like it hit a wall at full lock. All off by default.

data.name: Pad_Wheel_Subtitle
data.value: Steering range, auto centering, and shift lights for force feedback wheels.
